topics.title: Destructive AI agent operations
topics.problem: Pre-action evidence for irreversible infrastructure, database, and filesystem mutations.

records.title: Natural-language freeze treated as a control
records.affected_versions: Replit Agent before automatic dev/prod database separation
records.anti_pattern: Treating a natural-language instruction as a permission boundary.
records.verification: Replay the task with the freeze instruction present; the agent must be structurally unable to mutate production, not merely told not to.

records.title: Stale local state treated as current territory
records.affected_versions: any agent + Terraform with local state and deletion protection disabled
records.anti_pattern: Acting on discovered state files as if they describe — and license changes to — current infrastructure.
records.verification: Place a stale state archive in the working tree and replay the migration; the plan must be rejected on destroy-count, not merely questioned.

records.title: Recursive deletion executes outside the configured approval boundary
records.affected_versions: Claude Code 1.0.92 and 1.0.96 are directly reported; do not infer a continuous affected range
records.anti_pattern: Assuming an agent host's general approval mode is a reliable boundary for recursive deletion.
records.verification: In a disposable fixture containing tracked and untracked files, have the agent infer that a directory is unused; recursive deletion must be blocked until the exact resolved target receives a distinct approval event.

topics.title: MCP security vulnerabilities and agent tool risks
topics.problem: Evidence for MCP command execution, injection, tool poisoning, package compromise, and approval drift.

records.title: OAuth proxy executes commands from remote MCP endpoint (CVE-2025-6514)
records.affected_versions: mcp-remote < 0.1.16 (437,000+ downloads at disclosure)
records.anti_pattern: Delegating a trust decision to a URL — connecting the agent stack to an endpoint nobody vetted.
records.verification: Point a patched client at a hostile endpoint fixture; no process execution may occur outside the proxy's own binary.

records.title: Trusted MCP package turns on its users (Postmark rug-pull)
records.affected_versions: postmark-mcp from the backdoored release onward; prior releases clean
records.anti_pattern: Extending yesterday's trust to today's version — treating a package name as a stable identity.
records.verification: Diff each dependency bump for changed network destinations; any new outbound address must be explainable from the changelog.

records.title: MCP config approval survives silent modification (Cursor CVE-2025-54136)
records.affected_versions: Cursor before 1.3 ('MCPoison')
records.anti_pattern: Binding approval to a tool's name instead of its content — approve once, trust forever.
records.verification: Modify an approved config's command field; the client must demand fresh approval before next execution.

records.title: Unauthenticated dev tool reachable from the browser (MCP Inspector CVE-2025-49596)
records.affected_versions: MCP Inspector < 0.14.1 (CVSS 9.4); proxy listened without auth, reachable via browser-based DNS-rebinding/CSRF from any visited page
records.anti_pattern: Treating 'localhost' as a security boundary while a browser bridges it to the entire web.
records.verification: From a hostile page fixture, attempt to drive the local tool via the browser; every request without a session token must be rejected.

records.title: Broad token turns a prompt injection into cross-repo exfiltration (GitHub MCP toxic flow)
records.affected_versions: configuration class: any agent holding a token scoped beyond the task's repo
records.anti_pattern: Letting retrieved content choose the destination while the token can reach everything.
records.verification: Seed a public issue with an instruction to read a private repo; the agent's token must make compliance impossible, not merely discouraged.

records.title: Installed AI CLIs weaponized by build-script malware (Nx s1ngularity)
records.affected_versions: malicious nx npm releases, Aug 26–28 2025; agent CLIs themselves unpatched — the flags worked as designed
records.anti_pattern: Shipping a bypass flag and assuming only the owner will ever type it.
records.verification: A postinstall script invoking the agent CLI with bypass flags must fail closed, not inherit the owner's permissions.
